children: Beginning on Dec. 6, Nasdaq, NYSE Arca, and Cboe EDGX are all planning to extend trading to 23 hours a day, five days a week, subject to final SEC approval.
We asked Seeking Alpha analysts
and
about the pros and cons of allowing near-continuous trading of U.S. equities.
: The transition toward a 24-hour market is not a matter of if but when. The first benefit is that more activity will be regulated and exchange structures will improve.

But there are other key advantages. Non-U.S. residents, for example, will see the time zone mismatch reduced, thus having better access to U.S. equities. Domestic residents will have access outside their daily working schedule. And price discovery could become more continuous, thus reducing gaps at the opening bell.
There are also some cons.

The first concern is that more opening hours don't necessarily mean more liquidity. For this development to work, incremental trading activity is needed. Second, companies will have to figure out how to release their earnings while the market is open (Berkshire's strategy to release their reports on Saturdays could soon find other followers).
For investors, there are some key actionable names. Stocks such as Cboe Global Markets
, Nasdaq
, and Intercontinental Exchange
are direct beneficiaries, but also smaller companies such as Equinix
and Digital Realty Trust
, two REITs, could do well. Broadridge Financial Solutions
and Virtu Financial
also belong to the basket that could benefit from this change.

Though now widely discussed, I think investors should be aware of a key transformation that opens up yet another opportunity in key infrastructure stocks that work as chokepoints of flows and volumes. In a market where everyone focuses on AI, this is truly the underfollowed opportunity that could lead, if well-played, to interesting gains.

Jack Bowman: For the retail investor, the major pro will be that they're no longer beholden to traditional market hours to get their trades filled, which will enable those who can't trade during regular market hours. But that's not a huge segment of the population, I imagine.

The first con is that the change won't bring liquidity on its own, as demand for overnight trading is pretty thin outside institutions. Compound that with 23/5 hours, meaning liquidity will be even more spread out with more opportunities in the day to trade.
The change will definitely be a boon for the exchanges, who will make their cut off increased market maker activity during the extended hours. Nasdaq
immediately comes to mind, but I expect this to be a win for the NYSE
as well.
I also expect derivatives volume to increase, benefiting firms like Cboe Global Markets
and CME
, as cross-security hedging is more viable when both the derivatives exchanges and stock markets are open at the same time.

title: SA Asks: What are the pros and cons of allowing 23-hour US equities trading?
